newsitem.title: USA: Actor Burt Reynolds files for bankruptcy.
newsitem.headline: Actor Burt Reynolds files for bankruptcy.

text.p: Actor Burt Reynolds on Monday filed for Chapter 11 protection under federal bankruptcy laws, declaring debts of more than $10 million, his attorney said.

Reynolds, 58, is best-known for his roles on the television programme "Evening Shade" and the movies, "Deliverance" and "Smokey and the Bandit." He was divorced from actress Loni Anderson more than a year ago and owns a ranch and dinner theatre near Jupiter in south Florida.

Mark Bloom, an attorney for Reynolds, said the actor decided to file for protection under bankruptcy laws to win some "breathing space to focus on his career" and come up with a plan to repay his creditors.

"It's not unusual for an individual who is having temporary business problems to propose a plan under Chapter 11 to pay his creditors more than they would receive under a Chapter 7 liquidation," Bloom said.

The bankruptcy petition listed debts of more than $10 million, and Bloom said Reynolds had assets of "slightly less than $10 million." The debts, which include some disputed ones, are due to unprofitable business investments.

"This will not affect any of his obligations under the divorce settlement," Bloom said. "He intends to honour all of those obligations. He has never missed a child support payment, and he never will."
Reynolds most recently appeared in the Hollywood movie, "Striptease," based on a book by a Florida author.
